$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for iOS colour tokens.
Mirrored into: (a) the Figma file 'Passkey Vault — iOS Design System' collection 'PV Color',
NOTHING auto-syncs Figma -> .xcassets. This file is the join. Edit here, then re-run the generator.
Every light value was derived in OKLCH (hue and chroma preserved, lightness reduced) until it
reached WCAG AA 4.5:1 against surface/default light (#FFFFFF). The raw web palette in
docs/UI-DESIGN.md is tuned for dark surfaces and fails AA on light ones — teal at 2.02:1 and
amber at 1.66:1 are the extremes. Do not 'restore' the web values here without re-checking contrast.

tokens.note: Page background. Unchanged from the existing catalog.
Cards, list cells, sheets. Unchanged.
NEW. Middle elevation step for grouped-list section backgrounds. Dark is the base-200 #212121 the catalog was missing entirely — it jumped #1F1F1F straight to #262626.
Body text. Unchanged.
Secondary text. Unchanged; already AA in both modes.

CHANGED (rebrand coral -> mandarynka, 2026-08-18). Web's brand moved to #FD7235 / oklch(71% 0.1849 42) (was #E16540 / oklch(65.31% 0.1637 37.22)). Light re-derived by holding hue 42 / chroma 0.1849 and reducing lightness in OKLCH (gamut-mapped, CSS-Color-4 style: chroma binary-searched down at fixed L/H rather than per-channel clipped) until it cleared 4.5:1 on #FFFFFF -- landed at L=58.5% -> #CD4C00, measured 4.536:1 (previously #C94F2A at 4.53:1 on the old hue). Dark did NOT need re-lightening this time: the brand mandarynka itself (#FD7235) already measures 5.502:1 on #262626 -- higher than the old coral's own 4.42:1 there -- so the dark accent is the literal brand value, unlike before when #E36742 had to be synthesized. This one value serves as text on surface AND as a primary button fill under white.

Re-verified against mandarynka (2026-08-18); values UNCHANGED. UI-DESIGN.md defines this as 'Primary content #421300' (moved off white for the same reason below) with a single value — still incomplete for iOS, because the two roles of the accent pull in opposite directions in dark mode. PVAccent dark is now the literal brand fill (#FD7235, lighter than the old synthesized #E36742), so white on it is WORSE, not better: measured 2.751:1, still failing. The existing dark label #1F1F1F measures 5.993:1 on the new dark accent (up from 4.93:1 against the old #E36742) and continues to pass. Light mode knocks out in white (4.536:1 on the new light accent, passes), dark mode knocks out in near-black. Discovered by whiteLabelOnAccentFillMeetsWcagAaInBothAppearances failing against a hardcoded white.

CHANGED (rebrand coral -> mandarynka, 2026-08-18). The literal brand mandarynka from UI-DESIGN.md (was #E16540, now #FD7235 / oklch(71% 0.1849 42)), preserved for decorative fills only. Measured 2.751:1 on white -- DOWN from the old coral's 3.42:1, and now BELOW the 3:1 WCAG large-text/UI floor as well as the 4.5:1 AA text floor. This is the same fact UI-DESIGN.md records for the web's Primary content colour (white on the new primary is 2.75:1, which is why web moved Primary content to #421300). On iOS PVAccentBold is not currently used as text anywhere in the app (grep confirms zero non-test usages); this note narrows its licence accordingly -- decorative fills and icons only, never bound to text at ANY size, not even large text.
NEW. Passkey / passwordless — semantically the most brand-load-bearing token in the product, and it did not exist on iOS at all. Web teal #00CDB7 is 2.02:1 on white.
NEW. Strong password, no breach detected.
NEW. Old or reused password. Web amber #FFBE00 is 1.66:1 on white — the worst offender in the palette.
Unchanged. The light value was already hand-picked in this catalog at 4.80:1; kept over the derived #DC3545 because it is slightly more conservative. This is the precedent the whole approach follows.
NEW. Neutral notices.
NEW. Links and info accents (UI-DESIGN.md calls this 'secondary').

NEW (38-06). The favicon icon tile's ground -- deliberately the SAME value in both appearances, mirroring web's --pv-tile-bg. GitHub's favicon is black and vanishes on a dark tile (found in live review, packages/pv-ui/components/ItemIconTile.tsx's own comment); this token exists precisely so the favicon tile never follows PVSurfaceAlt into dark mode's #212121. Not a text-bearing surface, so no contrast_min.

NEW (38-06 dock). The dimming layer behind the dock's + panel, applied at PVMetrics.dockScrimOpacity (0.35 -- the HIG's own figure for a dark dimming layer over bright content behind Clear glass). A TOKEN and not `.black` because scripts/audit-ios-colour-tokens.sh check 1 bars literal colours outright; the generator writes alpha 1.000 for every token by construction, so the translucency lives in code. Light is a WARM near-black rather than neutral: dimming the cream #FCFBFA background toward pure black cools the whole surface and the product's temperature is its identity. Dark is true black, because #1F1F1F dimmed toward a warm black barely moves. Decorative -- it is never a text ground, so no contrast_min.

NEW (40, detail-conformance fix). The inset hairline between `.d`/`.r` rows inside a `.grp` card -- screens-vault.html's `--pv-sep: rgba(60,60,67,.20)` light / `rgba(235,235,245,.20)` dark (lines 58, 62), applied at PVMetrics.detailSeparatorOpacity (0.20) in code for the same reason as PVScrim above: the generator writes alpha 1.000 for every token, so the translucency lives in code, not the colorset. These exact RGB values are also iOS's own `UIColor.separator` hue (just a different alpha, 0.20 vs system's 0.29) -- a token rather than `Color(.separator)` directly so the hairline is drift-checked by --check like every other colour in this catalog, and so its opacity stays exactly the one the drawing specifies rather than whatever the OS ships next. Decorative -- never a text ground, so no contrast_min.

NEW (38-06). Literal third-party brand mark colour, transcribed from packages/pv-ui/components/ItemIconTile.tsx's CardBrandTile -- not part of the PV semantic palette, exempt from the design system's own AA gate the way a logo mark is. Fixed in both appearances (web does not flip Visa's tile either).

NEW (38-06). Same provenance as PVCardBrandVisa. Web additionally flips this tile's background to a light neutral in its dark theme (Tailwind `[[data-theme=vault-dark]_&]:bg-zinc-100`); iOS keeps the single light-theme value in both appearances for now -- a recorded, deliberate visual-parity simplification, not a security or functional gap (38-06-SUMMARY.md).
NEW (38-06). Same provenance as PVCardBrandVisa.
NEW (38-06). Same provenance as PVCardBrandMastercard -- web flips this one's background to zinc-100 in dark theme too; iOS keeps the single light-theme value (same recorded simplification).

NEW (38-06). The wordmark colour ON the four card-brand tiles above -- fixed white in both appearances because the tiles themselves are fixed brand colours that do not follow the system appearance (unlike PVOnAccent, which deliberately DOES flip because PVAccent itself flips). Exists so `scripts/audit-ios-colour-tokens.sh` check 1's blanket `.white` prohibition has a real token to point at instead of a literal.
